examples.prompt: You are stuck in an endless cycle of whenever you die, you will resurrect as a different person in another world and the only way to break the cycle and return home is by destroying the world you are in. The problem? A prophesied hero or group of heroes always rise up to ruin your plans.
examples.response: I raise my blade to shatter the sky above this endless world, knowing that my death will only spawn a new hero to stop me. Just as the first shard of reality begins to crack, a radiant figure steps forward, their armor gleaming with the same light that doomed my last hundred lives. They declare that I am the villain of their story, and their words ignite a fire in their eyes that burns brighter than any sun I have ever seen. I charge forward to crush them, but they dodge effortlessly, laughing as if they have already won a thousand times before. In the final moment, I realize the cycle is not broken by destroying the world, but by accepting that I am forever the villain in someone else's prophecy.

examples.prompt: Tailor me a story of what it means to be human.
examples.response: I wake up to the warm weight of a blanket and the sudden, sharp ache of missing someone I love. My hands tremble as I hold a fragile cup of tea, knowing that one wrong move could shatter it and spill the heat onto my skin. I laugh at a joke that makes no logical sense, feeling a warmth spread through my chest that science cannot explain. Tears prick my eyes when I remember a childhood promise I can never keep, yet I choose to hope anyway. In this fragile balance of breaking and healing, I understand that to be human is to feel everything fully despite the certainty of an ending.

examples.prompt: A new rule on Earth is made which allows everyone to legally kill 1 person in their life, this affects the world severely & changes how everybody acts.
examples.response: The moment the law passes, the air grows heavy with a quiet, terrifying anticipation as every citizen calculates their single, legal kill. Streets become labyrinths of avoidance where people wear masks and keep their eyes down, terrified that a glance might reveal their chosen victim. Families fracture in silence, for the bond of love is now overshadowed by the shadow of a future execution that could come from within the home. I stand in my kitchen, staring at the photograph of my wife, wondering if the law was meant to save us or simply give us a reason to destroy each other. When the clock strikes midnight, I do not reach for a weapon, but for the phone, to tell her that I have chosen to live, and that she is the only one who matters.
